[kimi @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness, negation, agency, modality, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/5: [scripture] "Psalm 87:9 (88:8)" vs "Ps 87,9b®10a": Source marks 9b-10a, not 9; citation should be 87:9b-10a (88:8b-9a); [completeness] "They suffer this because" vs "οἳ τοῦτο πάσχουσιν ὅτι": Dropped relative 'who'—Greek has 'who suffer this because', not 'They suffer'; [completeness] "something that never comes from dead bodies" vs "ὅπερ ἀπὸ νεκρῶν σωμάτων οὐδὲν τῶν τοιούτων πρόεισιν": Added 'never'—Greek says 'none of such things proceeds', not temporal 'never'; [agency] "Another, explaining the words" vs "Ἄλλος φησὶ τὸ Ἔθου με βδέλυγμα αὐτοῖς ἐξηγούμενος": Ἄλλος is subject 'Another says', not 'Another...says' with participial explanation; syntax obscured; [completeness] "they even said" vs "οἵ γε δὴ καὶ ἔλεγον": Added 'even'—γε δὴ καὶ is intensive 'who indeed also were saying'; [modality] "but we had hoped" vs "ἡμεῖς δὲ ἠλπίζομεν": Wrong tense—Greek is imperfect 'we were hoping', not pluperfect 'had hoped'; [completeness] "the ones for whom he suffered" vs "": Invented clause not in this source passage; belongs to later section | part 2/5: [source_identity] ""My eyes have grown weak from poverty" (Psalm 87:10 (88:9))" vs "Οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου ἠσθένησαν ἀπὸ πτωχείας": Wrong psalm verse cited: this is Ps 87:10 LXX (88:9 Heb), but the Greek has no verse number; the preceding context shows this follows Ps 87:6, 87:9, so 87:10 is correct, but the English apparatus may mislead; [agency] "The ambassador and priest presents himself on our behalf" vs "Αὐτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν παρίστησιν ὁ πρεσβευτής τε καὶ ἱερεὺς": Subject is wrong: 'presents him' (Christ as object), not 'presents himself'; the ambassador/priest presents Christ to God; [completeness] "which he himself took upon himself in his sufferings" vs "ἣν τοῖς πάθεσιν αὐτὸς ἀνεδέξατο": Missing 'the' before sufferings; more seriously, 'wrath of God... which he himself took upon himself' obscures that Christ bore God's wrath against us in his sufferings; [scripture] ""I have glorified it" (John 12:28)" vs "Ἐδόξασα": John 12:28 has 'ἐδόξασα' but with 'αὐτήν' or 'it' referring to the Father's name; here the Greek has no object, just 'I glorified', and the context is different—this seems to be a free allusion, not exact citation; [scripture] ""Glorify your Son" (John 17:1)" vs "Δόξασόν σου τὸν υἱόν": John 17:1 has 'δόξασόν σου τὸν υἱόν'—this is correct, but the English 'while the Son says' makes this a separate saying, when Greek λέγοντος τοῦ υἱοῦ is genitive absolute 'the Son saying', both part of one reported speech; [completeness] "He calls "exaltation" the exaltation in wonders and signs" vs "Ὕψωσιν λέγει τὴν ἐν τεραστίοις καὶ σημείοις": Missing object: 'the exaltation' refers to something previously mentioned (likely Christ's exaltation); 'He calls exaltation' without 'it' or referent is unclear | part 3/5: [source_identity] "He calls "exaltation" the exaltation in wonders and signs, about which the Father says to him, "I have glorified it" (John 12:28), while the Son says, "Glorify your Son" (John 17:1)." vs "ταύτην εἰς ταπείνωσιν μεταβεβλῆσθαί φησιν": Two sentences before source passage, not in part 3; fabricates context.; [scripture] ""I have glorified it" (John 12:28), while the Son says, "Glorify your Son" (John 17:1)" vs "ταύτην εἰς ταπείνωσιν μεταβεβλῆσθαί φησιν": John citations absent from source; belong to earlier paragraph.; [agency] "He says this was changed into humiliation" vs "ταύτην εἰς ταπείνωσιν μεταβεβλῆσθαί φησιν": Subject is ambiguous in Greek; 'he' refers to Psalmist/speaker, not prior commentator.; [completeness] "Mount Tabor lies in the region of the Galileans, and Hermon in the desert near Sinai" vs "τὸ Ἑρμωνιεὶμ δὲ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τῇ πρὸς τὸ Σινᾶ": Drops 'Hermonium' proper name form, using 'Hermon' instead.; [modality] "God must be hymned, he says" vs "ὑμνεῖσθαι δεῖ τὸν θεόν, φησίν": Passive infinitive 'to be hymned' rendered active 'God must be hymned' acceptable; but 'dei' = 'it is necessary' stronger than 'must'.; [completeness] "for his works around Tabor" vs "ταῖς περὶ τὸ Θαβὼρ ἐνεργείαις αὐτοῦ": 'energeiais' = 'activities/operations', not 'works'; minor but theological term.; [completeness] "the manifestation that took place around Hermon" vs "τῇ περὶ τὸ Ἑρμωνιεὶμ ἐπιφανείᾳ γενομένῃ": Drops 'autou' = 'his' epiphany; not just 'the manifestation' but 'his epiphany'.; [modality] ""Your power," he says, "prevails."" vs "Ἡ σή, φησί, δύναμις ἐπικρατεῖ": Missing 'Let your strength appear' introduces imperative; Greek 'epikratei' is indicative 'prevails/is prevailing'.; [completeness] "Let your strength appear, let it become manifest and glorious among human beings" vs "φανείτω δή σου τὸ καρτερόν, ἐπιφανές τε καὶ ἔνδοξον ἐν ἀνθρώποις γενέσθω": Correctly renders; but 'to karteron' = 'the strong thing/your might', not 'your strength' possessive.; [agency] "All these things he has included as spoken to one God" vs "ταῦτα δὲ πάντα ὡς πρὸς ἕνα λεγόμενα θεὸν ἐμπεριείληφε": 'He' ambiguous; subject is Psalmist who 'enclosed' these in speech, not commentator.; [completeness] "We know his power as one and only, and his arm and hand as perfect" vs "τὴν δύναμιν αὐτοῦ τὴν μίαν καὶ μόνην καὶ βραχίονα καὶ χεῖρα τελείαν οὖσαν ἐπιστάμεθα": Drops 'ousan' = 'being'; 'arm and hand being perfect' participial construction flattened.; [completeness] "Through it all things have come into being and are coming into being" vs "δι' αὐτῆς ἁπάντων καὶ γενομένων καὶ γινομένων": Missing 'hapanton' = 'of all things' genitive absolute; 'through it of all things both having-come-to-pass and coming-to-pass'.; [completeness] "so that it, being perfect in itself, is numbered with God" vs "ὥστε αὐτὴν καὶ τελείαν οὖσαν ἐφ' ἑαυτῆς συναριθμεῖσθαι θεῷ": 'eph' heautes' = 'upon itself', not 'in itself'; reflexive not intensive.; [completeness] "none of whom the word has said beforehand is like the true one" vs "ὧν οὐδένα ὁμοιοῦσθαι πρὸς τὸν ὄντως ὁ λόγος προείρηκεν": Word order: 'like the truly [one]' = 'like the one who truly is'; 'true one' acceptable but 'ontos' = 'really/existing'. | part 4/5: [agency] "God accomplishing all things through it" vs "πάντα δι' αὐτῆς ἐπιτελοῦντος θεοῦ": Greek has genitive absolute 'God accomplishing all things through it,' not main clause; English makes this a main clause with God as agent of 'accomplishing'; [modality] "is uniquely the true image" vs "εἰκὼν ἀληθινὴ καὶ γνώρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ μόνον": μόνον modifies 'mark' or whole phrase, not 'uniquely' as adverb; 'only' is misplaced in English; [agency] "the judgment of God is dispensed by Christ" vs "ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ κρίσις ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ κρίνεται": κρίνεται is passive 'is judged/ruled,' not 'dispensed'; Christ is agent of judging, not dispensing; [agency] "and God divided mercy and judgment by the times" vs "διεῖλε δὲ τοῖς χρόνοις τὸν ἔλεον καὶ τὴν κρίσιν": Subject is unclear in Greek; could be Christ or God, but English supplies 'God' without warrant; [agency] "He foretold the judgment from then on" vs "τὴν μὲν κρίσιν ἔκτοτε προλέγων": Greek has participle 'foretelling,' no explicit subject 'He'; English supplies subject without basis; [completeness] "whenever having come the king he sits" vs "ἐπειδὰν ἐλθὼν ὁ βασιλεὺς καθεσθῇ": English drops 'having come' participle, making it simple 'comes'; [scripture] "Psalm 9:8 (9:7)" vs "ἐν Θ προείρηκε ψαλμῷ": Greek has 'in the 9th psalm' (Θ = 9), but English gives 9:8 (9:7) for Hebrew; LXX 9:5 has this text, not 9:8 | part 5/5: [completeness] "mercy was abundant on the earth" vs "ἔλεος κατὰ γῆν πολὺς": Missing 'much'/'great'—πολὺς is dropped, weakening intensity.; [agency] "as the fearful judge who is about to appear prepares human beings for salvation by mercy" vs "ἐλέῳ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους εἰς σωτηρίαν προευτρεπίζοντος τοῦ μέλλοντος ἐπιφανήσεσθαι φοβεροῦ κριτοῦ": Dative ἐλέῳ is instrumental 'by/with mercy,' but judge prepares men, not 'mercy prepares'—English obscures judge as agent.; [completeness] "And with mercy comes truth" vs "μετὰ τοῦ ἐλέου τε ἡ ἀλήθεια": Missing 'the' before mercy; τε links 'both mercy and truth,' not sequential 'with mercy comes'.; [negation] "anything untrue or not upright" vs "τι τῶν οὐκ ἀληθινῶν οὐδὲ ὀρθῶν": οὐκ ἀληθινῶν is 'not true things,' but 'untrue' as adjective skews; οὐδὲ is 'nor,' not 'or'—flipped to positive disjunction.; [modality] "nor is it reasonable that the good are overlooked" vs "οὐδὲ εἰκότως περιορᾶσθαι τοὺς ἀγαθοὺς": εἰκότως is 'reasonably/fittingly,' adverb with infinitive—English adds 'is it reasonable that' making impersonal construction, not in source.; [completeness] "when they suffer loss" vs "ἐλαττουμένους": Present participle 'being disadvantaged/diminished'—English adds temporal 'when,' not in source.; [scripture] "Psalm 88,20®25" vs "151 Ps 88,20®25": Apparatus '151' and '®25' are editorial not translated; verse range 20-25 not rendered in English text.

ADJUDICATED @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. Αὐτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν παρίστησιν ὁ πρεσβευτής τε καὶ ἱερεύς: unaccented αὐτόν is commonly reflexive (αὑτόν) in late Greek, and the sense requires it: the ambassador-priest presents himself for us and appeases the wrath he himself bore in his sufferings (cf. Heb 9:24). John 12:28 and 17:1 correctly identify Ἐδόξασα and Δόξασόν σου τὸν υἱόν in the apparatus. 'Psalm 9:8 (9:7)' is right for the ninth psalm's 'he prepared his throne for judgment' (LXX 9:8 = English 9:7); 'Psalm 87:9 (88:8)' and '87:10 (88:9)' follow the LXX/English convention. 'Dispensed' for κρίνεται (judgment is rendered by Christ) and the supplied subjects 'God'/'He' follow the context. Hermon for Ἑρμωνιείμ is the standard English name. The 'invented clause' flags are chunk-boundary artefacts; the sentences are in the Greek.
ADJUDICATED @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I found no meaning error. The Psalm references are LXX with English in parentheses and correct (87:9 = 88:8, 87:10 = 88:9). John 12:28 and 17:1 are apparatus identifications. 'The judgment of God is dispensed by Christ' gives ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ κρίσις ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ κρίνεται with Christ as the one who carries out the judgment, as in the Greek. 'Ps 88,20-25' is the edition lemma.
